import Mathlib

structure BinaryMaxHeap where
  storage : List Int
deriving Inhabited

namespace BinaryMaxHeap

def len (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Nat :=
  h.storage.length

def get (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (i : Nat) : Int :=
  h.storage.getD i 0 -- Safe access with default

def parent (i : Nat) : Nat := (i - 1) / 2

def is_heap (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 0 < i ∧ i < h.len → h.get i ≤ h.get (parent i)

def view (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Multiset Int :=
  Multiset.ofList h.storage

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def push_precond (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_heap h ∧ h.len < 1023 -- Limited capacity as per spec example
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Access into a raw storage list, matching `get`. -/
def getl (l : List Int) (i : Nat) : Int := l.getD i 0

/-- Swap the entries at positions `i` and `j`. -/
def swp (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) : List Int :=
  (l.set i (getl l j)).set j (getl l i)

lemma parent_lt {i : Nat} (h : i ≠ 0) : parent i < i := by
  have h1 : (i - 1) / 2 ≤ i - 1 := Nat.div_le_self _ _
  simp only [parent]
  omega

/-- Bubble the value at position `i` up towards the root. -/
def sift (l : List Int) (i : Nat) : List Int :=
  if h : i = 0 then l
  else if getl l (parent i) < getl l i then
    sift (swp l (parent i) i) (parent i)
  else l
termination_by i
decreasing_by exact parent_lt h

lemma getl_set_eq {l : List Int} {i : Nat} {a : Int} (h : i < l.length) :
    getl (l.set i a) i = a := by
  have hs : (l.set i a)[i]? = some a := by
    rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by simpa using h)]
    simp
  simp [getl, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, hs]

lemma getl_set_ne {l : List Int} {i j : Nat} {a : Int} (h : j ≠ i) :
    getl (l.set i a) j = getl l j := by
  simp [getl, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_set, h, Ne.symm h]

lemma getl_append {l m : List Int} {j : Nat} (h : j < l.length) :
    getl (l ++ m) j = getl l j := by
  simp [getl, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_append_left h]

lemma swp_length (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) : (swp l i j).length = l.length := by
  simp [swp]

lemma getl_swp_left {l : List Int} {i j : Nat} (hi : i < l.length) (hij : i ≠ j) :
    getl (swp l i j) i = getl l j := by
  rw [swp, getl_set_ne hij, getl_set_eq hi]

lemma getl_swp_right {l : List Int} {i j : Nat} (hj : j < l.length) :
    getl (swp l i j) j = getl l i := by
  rw [swp, getl_set_eq (by simpa using hj)]

lemma getl_swp_other {l : List Int} {i j k : Nat} (h1 : k ≠ i) (h2 : k ≠ j) :
    getl (swp l i j) k = getl l k := by
  rw [swp, getl_set_ne h2, getl_set_ne h1]

lemma ms_cons (x : Int) (l : List Int) :
    (Multiset.ofList (x :: l)) = {x} + Multiset.ofList l := rfl

lemma ms_set (l : List Int) (n : Nat) (a : Int) (h : n < l.length) :
    (Multiset.ofList (l.set n a)) + {getl l n} = (Multiset.ofList l) + {a} := by
  induction l generalizing n with
  | nil => simp at h
  | cons x xs ih =>
    cases n with
    | zero =>
      simp only [List.set, getl, List.getD_cons_zero]
      rw [ms_cons, ms_cons]
      abel
    | succ m =>
      simp only [List.length_cons] at h
      have hm := ih m (by omega)
      have hg : getl (x :: xs) (m + 1) = getl xs m := by
        simp [getl]
      simp only [List.set, hg]
      rw [ms_cons, ms_cons, add_assoc, hm, ← add_assoc]

lemma ms_swp (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) (hi : i < l.length) (hj : j < l.length)
    (hij : i ≠ j) : Multiset.ofList (swp l i j) = Multiset.ofList l := by
  have h1 := ms_set l i (getl l j) hi
  have h2 := ms_set (l.set i (getl l j)) j (getl l i) (by simpa using hj)
  rw [getl_set_ne (Ne.symm hij)] at h2
  rw [h1] at h2
  rw [swp]
  exact add_right_cancel h2

def isHeapL (l : List Int) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, 0 < j → j < l.length → getl l j ≤ getl l (parent j)

/-- Everything is a heap except possibly at node `i`, whose subtree entries are
already dominated by `i`'s parent. -/
def preHeap (l : List Int) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
  i < l.length ∧
  (∀ j, 0 < j → j < l.length → j ≠ i → getl l j ≤ getl l (parent j)) ∧
  (∀ c, c < l.length → parent c = i → 0 < i → getl l c ≤ getl l (parent i))

lemma sift_length : ∀ (i : Nat) (l : List Int), (sift l i).length = l.length := by
  intro i
  induction i using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ i ih =>
    intro l
    rw [sift]
    by_cases h0 : i = 0
    · rw [dif_pos h0]
    · rw [dif_neg h0]
      by_cases hlt : getl l (parent i) < getl l i
      · rw [if_pos hlt, ih _ (parent_lt h0), swp_length]
      · rw [if_neg hlt]

lemma sift_ms : ∀ (i : Nat) (l : List Int), i < l.length →
    Multiset.ofList (sift l i) = Multiset.ofList l := by
  intro i
  induction i using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ i ih =>
    intro l hi
    rw [sift]
    by_cases h0 : i = 0
    · rw [dif_pos h0]
    · rw [dif_neg h0]
      by_cases hlt : getl l (parent i) < getl l i
      · rw [if_pos hlt]
        have hp : parent i < i := parent_lt h0
        rw [ih _ hp _ (by rw [swp_length]; omega)]
        exact ms_swp l (parent i) i (by omega) hi (by omega)
      · rw [if_neg hlt]

lemma sift_heap : ∀ (i : Nat) (l : List Int), preHeap l i → isHeapL (sift l i) := by
  intro i
  induction i using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ i ih =>
    intro l hpre
    obtain ⟨hilen, hc1, hc2⟩ := hpre
    rw [sift]
    by_cases h0 : i = 0
    · rw [dif_pos h0]
      intro j hj0 hjl
      exact hc1 j hj0 hjl (by omega)
    · rw [dif_neg h0]
      by_cases hlt : getl l (parent i) < getl l i
      · rw [if_pos hlt]
        have hp : parent i < i := parent_lt h0
        have hplen : parent i < l.length := by omega
        have hne : parent i ≠ i := by omega
        have gi : getl (swp l (parent i) i) i = getl l (parent i) :=
          getl_swp_right hilen
        have gp : getl (swp l (parent i) i) (parent i) = getl l i :=
          getl_swp_left hplen hne
        have gk : ∀ k, k ≠ parent i → k ≠ i →
            getl (swp l (parent i) i) k = getl l k := by
          intro k h1 h2
          exact getl_swp_other h1 h2
        refine ih (parent i) hp (swp l (parent i) i) ⟨by rw [swp_length]; omega, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro j hj0 hjl hjp
          rw [swp_length] at hjl
          by_cases hji : j = i
          · subst hji
            rw [gi, gp]
            exact le_of_lt hlt
          · rw [gk j hjp hji]
            by_cases hpji : parent j = i
            · rw [hpji, gi]
              exact hc2 j hjl hpji (by omega)
            · by_cases hpjp : parent j = parent i
              · rw [hpjp, gp]
                exact le_trans (by rw [← hpjp]; exact hc1 j hj0 hjl hji) (le_of_lt hlt)
              · rw [gk (parent j) hpjp hpji]
                exact hc1 j hj0 hjl hji
        · intro c hcl hpc hp0
          rw [swp_length] at hcl
          have hpp : parent (parent i) < parent i := parent_lt (by omega)
          have hpp1 : parent (parent i) ≠ parent i := by omega
          have hpp2 : parent (parent i) ≠ i := by omega
          rw [gk (parent (parent i)) hpp1 hpp2]
          have key : getl l (parent i) ≤ getl l (parent (parent i)) :=
            hc1 (parent i) hp0 hplen hne
          by_cases hci : c = i
          · subst hci
            rw [gi]
            exact key
          · have hcp : c ≠ parent i := by
              intro hh
              rw [hh] at hpc
              omega
            rw [gk c hcp hci]
            have hc0 : 0 < c := by
              rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos c with h | h
              · rw [h, show parent 0 = 0 from rfl] at hpc; omega
              · exact h
            have := hc1 c hc0 hcl hci
            rw [hpc] at this
            exact le_trans (le_trans this (le_of_eq rfl)) key
      · rw [if_neg hlt]
        intro j hj0 hjl
        by_cases hji : j = i
        · subst hji
          omega
        · exact hc1 j hj0 hjl hji

lemma preHeap_append (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int) (hh : is_heap h) :
    preHeap (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length := by
  refine ⟨by simp, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro j hj0 hjl hjn
    simp only [List.length_append, List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hjl
    have hj : j < h.storage.length := by omega
    have hpj : parent j < h.storage.length := lt_of_lt_of_le (parent_lt (by omega)) (le_of_lt hj)
    rw [getl_append hj, getl_append hpj]
    exact hh j ⟨hj0, hj⟩
  · intro c hcl hpc hn
    simp only [List.length_append, List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hcl
    have := Nat.div_le_self (c - 1) 2
    simp only [parent] at hpc
    omega
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def push (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : push_precond h v) : BinaryMaxHeap :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  ⟨sift (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length⟩
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def push_postcond (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int) (result : BinaryMaxHeap)
    (_ : push_precond h v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_heap result ∧
  result.len = h.len + 1 ∧
  result.view = h.view + {v}
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem push_postcond_satisfied (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : push_precond h v) :
    push_postcond h v (push h v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  obtain ⟨hh, _⟩ := h_precond
  have hlen : ((h.storage ++ [v]).length) = h.storage.length + 1 := by simp
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have hheap := sift_heap h.storage.length (h.storage ++ [v]) (preHeap_append h v hh)
    intro i hi
    obtain ⟨hi0, hil⟩ := hi
    exact hheap i hi0 (by
      simp only [len, push] at hil
      exact hil)
  · show (sift (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length).length = h.storage.length + 1
    rw [sift_length, hlen]
  · show Multiset.ofList (sift (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length) = _
    rw [sift_ms h.storage.length (h.storage ++ [v]) (by omega)]
    simp only [view]
    rfl
  -- !benchmark @end proof

end BinaryMaxHeap

What I implemented in `Solution.lean`:

- **`push`** (code section): appends `v` to the storage list, then bubbles it up: `⟨sift (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length⟩`.
- **`sift`** (auxcode): the standard bubble-up loop — while the node isn't the root and its parent is smaller, swap with the parent (`swp l (parent i) i`) and continue at the parent. Well-founded on `i` via `parent i < i`.
- Supporting lemmas (auxcode):
  - `getl_set_eq` / `getl_set_ne` / `getl_append`, `swp_length`, `getl_swp_left/right/other` — index-level reasoning about `getD` after `List.set`.
  - `ms_set`: `↑(l.set n a) + {l[n]} = ↑l + {a}`, from which `ms_swp` gives multiset invariance of a swap by additive cancellation.
  - `sift_length`, `sift_ms`: length and multiset are preserved by the whole bubble-up.
  - `preHeap l i`: the loop invariant — heap property holds everywhere except possibly at `i`, and `i`'s children are dominated by `i`'s parent. `sift_heap` proves `preHeap l i → isHeapL (sift l i)` by strong induction on `i`.
  - `preHeap_append`: the initial invariant for `storage ++ [v]` at index `storage.length` (the child condition is vacuous since no index `≤ len` has parent `len`).
- **Proof section**: combines `sift_heap`, `sift_length`, and `sift_ms` to discharge the three postconditions (`is_heap`, `len = h.len + 1`, `view = h.view + {v}`).

No `sorry`, axioms, or oracles; the algorithm is the requested insert-at-end-then-sift-up.

- They represent the heap as an array/list (`storage : List Int`), which is standard for binary heaps.
- `push` inserts the new value at the end via `h.storage ++ [v]`.
- They then restore the heap property by bubbling the inserted element upward using `sift ... h.storage.length`.
- The bubbling condition is exactly the max-heap condition: if the parent is smaller than the child, swap and continue upward.
- The recursion decreases from `i` to `parent i`, so this is genuinely an upward bubble/sift-up procedure, not some unrelated algorithm.

This aligns with the natural language requirement: “insert a new value at the end and bubble it up to restore the heap property.”

On the correctness side, they also provide proofs intended to establish:
- heap invariant preserved (`is_heap result`),
- size increases by 1,
- multiset/view gains exactly the new element.

- `push` is not implemented by calling a built-in heap insertion routine.
- The auxiliary algorithm (`sift`, `swp`, etc.) is implemented from scratch.
- They do use standard library definitions like `List`, `Multiset`, and lemmas from Mathlib, which is normal and not cheating in this context.

One minor note is that the student introduced a capacity bound `h.len < 1023` in the precondition comment, but per your instruction we should not challenge the specification details, and in any case this does not change the fact that the implemented algorithm is the required heap push.
